sections.content: visel ('to wear') is a regular verb: the first-person singular takes -ek, like most verbs whose stem ends in a consonant. What is worn is the direct object and takes the accusative -t.

items.english: I wear a shirt and a jumper.

sections.content: Don't forget the accusative on the clothing item: 'inget', not 'ing' -- visel always needs an object marked with -t, just like kér and keres.
